method: Headlines collected via web search (fetch_news.py collector blocked in sandbox; use it for local/Actions runs). Entity sentiment scored by Claude during the weekly Cowork routine. sentiment = 0-100 D-favorability of coverage tone (matches existing dashboard sentimentScore semantics: >55 leans D, <45 leans R). candidateSentiment = 0-100 favorability of coverage toward that candidate personally. outletLean: -2 left ... +2 right (AllSides-style); null = unrated outlet, excluded from scatter.

races.matchup: Susan Collins (R, inc.) vs. Troy Jackson (D)
races.summary: Coverage in the last two weeks centers on polls showing five-term incumbent Susan Collins slipping into a virtual tie or trailing Democrat Troy Jackson, with a Fox News survey putting Jackson up 48-46 and reporting broadly framed around Collins's votes aligning with an unpopular Trump. Reporting emphasizes Jackson's competitiveness and Collins's vulnerability, while noting his progressive positions as a line of Republican attack.

In a competitive Maine Senate race, women voters could be the deciders
Does Troy Jackson stand a chance against Susan Collins?

races.matchup: Hannah Pingree (D) vs. Bobby Charles (R) vs. Rick Bennett (I)
races.summary: Newest datable coverage is from July; no substantive general-election news on/after 2026-08-15 was found. That coverage shows Democrat Hannah Pingree with a commanding lead (~50-36 over Bobby Charles, with Rick Bennett ~8%) and dominating fundraising, plus debate-scheduling stories. Tone favors Pingree as the clear front-runner to succeed term-limited Gov. Janet Mills.

Tone tilts slightly Democratic on El-Sayed's polling advantage, though outlets stress a toss-up.

races.summary: Coverage centers on data centers becoming the defining issue, with a leaked internal GOP memo warning the backlash could cost Husted the seat; Brown has made opposition to data-center tax breaks his centerpiece and leads or ties in recent polling. Tone leans modestly Democratic.

races.summary: Despite a Democratic-leaning environment, incumbent Ayotte is bucking the tide: an Aug 17-18 Saint Anselm poll has her up 49-38 (widening from June), with a 51% favorable rating while Warmington sits underwater. Warmington centers her campaign on affordability; Ayotte attacks Warmington's past work for Purdue Pharma. Tone leans slightly Republican.

Trump-endorsed Kansas Senate President Ty Masterson won a seven-way GOP field (~43%), while Overland Park state Sen. Cindy Holscher won the Democratic nomination over Ethan Corson (~49-39). Coverage was largely neutral primary reporting; outlets framed Kansas as a top GOP gubernatorial pickup opportunity. Little fresh coverage since.

races.matchup: Kurt Alme (R) vs. Alani Bankhead (D) vs. Seth Bodnar (I)
races.summary: This open-seat race (Daines not running; he endorsed former U.S. Attorney Kurt Alme) is defined by a three-way split on the left. After the Aug 10 withdrawal deadline, Democrat Alani Bankhead vowed to stay in despite party pressure to clear the field for independent Seth Bodnar. Polling shows Alme leading (~45%) with Bodnar (~30%) and Bankhead (~15%) dividing the anti-GOP vote. Tone unfavorable to Democratic prospects.

GOP House Speaker Lisa Demuth upset Trump-endorsed Mike Lindell and is treated as a credible challenger.
